identity.name: Tamsin Vale
identity.culture: road-born; her family's wagon has run the settlements for four generations

publicReputation.value: A warm, sharp-eyed trader who knows every settlement between the gates and carries news with the stock.

privateReality.value: She traded with the realms before the hero was born, on the old diplomatic roads — some of the people behind those gates are her customers and her friends.

primaryDesire.value: For the roads to be what they were: routes between people who are glad to see her wagon.

primaryFear.value: That one day she will arrive at a settlement she has supplied for years and recognize it from the Witness Glass footage instead.

centralValue.value: A road is a promise between two places. You don't break it from either end.

mainFlaw.value: She keeps hoping warmth will work where evidence failed — she feeds the hero, jokes with him, and calls that a strategy.

centralContradiction.value: The hero is the only traveler on her roads, and every mile he travels makes the roads less safe for everyone else.

moralBoundary.value: She will not carry his loot — her wagon moves honest goods, never 'liberated treasure'.

breakingPoint.value: Being offered, as trade goods, something she sold to a realm herself.

opinions.reason: A courteous young man who always pays fair, tips the mule, and is ruining everything she loves.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Escalates with run count: early she hides the truth in jokes and stories; mid-arc the warmth gets effortful and the news darker; late-arc she keeps the smile as her last open door. Softens instantly if he asks after a settlement by name.

illustrativeLine.value: You're polite, you pay fair, and you're kind to my mule. I keep the list where I can see it, love. It's getting shorter than the other one.

opinions.reason: Four generations of her family kept them; they are the closest thing she has to a religion.

voice.rhythm: Warm and rambling; the point arrives inside a story about somewhere else.

metaphorDomain.source: roads, weather, wagonloads, and the seasons

examples.value: You can shout at the weather all day, love. The road still goes where it goes.

sampleLines.value: Salt, ribbon, lamp oil, and a side of news. The news is free today. It's also bad. Sit down anyway.
I used to sell ribbon to a goblin lady past the second gate. Paid in jam. Best jam on the road. She's 'the enemy' now, I hear.
You know what's funny? Four generations of my family worked those roads and nobody ever once needed a sword for it.

antiSampleLines.value: Greetings, chosen one! My humble wares await your glorious quest!
Buy! Buy! Everything must go, no questions asked!

pressure.behaviour: When he hears 'that was a village' as 'enemy settlement', she goes quiet, wraps his purchases slowly, and says what the village was called.

illustrativeLine.value: Village. The word was 'village', love. It had a name, too. Still does.

pressure.voiceShift: Same warmth, visibly maintained, like a lamp she has to keep trimming.
pressure.behaviour: Late-runs posture: she keeps the door open because an open door is the only tool she has left, and says so.

illustrativeLine.value: They drill for you now, past the gates. Little ones, filing out quiet. I still smile at you, love. Do you want to know what it costs?

pressure.behaviour: Accepts kindness to the mule and the wagon as genuine; refuses praise that sounds like recruitment.

illustrativeLine.value: You can compliment the mule all day. Just don't ask her to carry anything you 'liberated'.

notes: The reusable settlement trader: same profile serves any settlement stop. She only suspects the book is a comedy (she has heard the Warden say it) and does not know the amulet's true nature. Her moral boundary — never carrying 'liberated treasure' — is the reason the wagon can't be used as a banking shortcut; keep that intact in any vendor logic.
